trips.title: Andaman Tropical (5N/6D)
trips.description: Escape to the pristine archipelago of the Andaman and Nicobar Islands, where powdery white coral sands merge into turquoise waters and dense tropical rainforests. Begin in Port Blair with an evocative journey through Indian freedom struggle history at the historic Cellular Jail, capped by its poignant evening Light and Sound show. Board an air-conditioned luxury catamaran across the open ocean to Havelock Island (Swaraj Dweep). Sunkissed hours await at Asia's celebrated Radhanagar Beach, consistently rated among the world's most breathtaking coastlines for its epic crimson sunsets, and at Elephant Beach with its vibrant fringing coral reefs teeming with marine life. Journey onward to peaceful Neil Island (Shaheed Dweep) to wander across the natural geological wonder of Howrah Bridge and relax on Bharatpur and Laxmanpur beaches. Complete with inter-island cruise transfers, verified beachfront four-star resorts, daily breakfasts and dinners, and round-the-clock island coordination, this tropical getaway guarantees an extraordinary island reverie.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Port Blair & Historic Cellular Jail Light Show
itinerary.description: Land at Veer Savarkar International Airport in Port Blair, greeted by ocean air and tropical warmth. Meet your private island escort and transfer to your seaside resort. After relaxing, visit the national memorial of Cellular Jail in the afternoon. Walk through its historic central tower and solitary confinement wings where Indian freedom fighters made untold sacrifices. At dusk, witness the deeply moving Light and Sound show narrating the epic struggle for independence under a star-filled island sky. Enjoy a coastal seafood dinner at your resort.

itinerary.title: Catamaran Cruise to Havelock & Radhanagar Sunset
itinerary.description: After an early breakfast, transfer to Phoenix Bay Jetty to board a high-speed luxury private catamaran (Makruzz or Green Ocean) bound for Havelock Island. Watch flying fish leap alongside the ship as you cruise across the deep blue Andaman Sea. Arrive at Havelock Jetty, transfer to your beachfront resort, and settle in among swaying coconut palms. In the late afternoon, head to world-renowned Radhanagar Beach (Beach No. 7). Walk along the wide white sands, swim in warm crystalline waters, and watch an unforgettable fiery sunset over the horizon.

itinerary.title: Elephant Beach Coral Reef Exploration & Water Sports
itinerary.description: Set out by speedboat in the morning to Elephant Beach, famous for its thriving near-shore coral reefs. Strap on snorkel gear or board a glass-bottom boat to witness vibrant brain corals, sea anemones, and schools of colorful clownfish and parrotfish gliding through warm tropical water. Thrill-seekers can try tandem jet skiing, banana boat rides, or undersea walking. Return to your resort by midday for an afternoon at leisure lounging by the pool or bicycling through village lanes. Relish a romantic candlelit dinner by the shore.

itinerary.title: Havelock to Neil Island: Natural Bridge & Laxmanpur Sunset
itinerary.description: Board a morning ferry from Havelock across to tranquil Neil Island (Shaheed Dweep), the vegetable bowl of the Andamans. Check in to your eco-resort and set off to explore the geological wonder of the Natural Rock Formation, locally known as Howrah Bridge, revealed during low tide along the dead coral beds. Continue to Laxmanpur Beach in the evening, a secluded white sand beach famous for its deep orange sunsets and scattered decorative seashells. Enjoy a relaxed tropical island dinner under the palms.

itinerary.title: Bharatpur Beach Coral Lagoon & Return to Port Blair
itinerary.description: Spend a peaceful morning at Bharatpur Beach, renowned for its crystal-clear shallow lagoon and gentle turquoise waves ideal for swimming and glass-bottom coral viewing. Later, transfer to Neil Jetty for your return catamaran voyage back to Port Blair. Arrive by afternoon and check into your hotel. Spend the evening browsing Aberdeen Bazaar for unique Andaman sea-shell souvenirs, coconut shell lamps, and local island honey before a special farewell coastal dinner featuring fresh catch of the day.

itinerary.title: Port Blair Farewell & Airport Departure
itinerary.description: Enjoy your final island breakfast with tropical fruits overlooking the Bay of Bengal. Take in the fresh ocean breeze and capture last photos of the palm-fringed shoreline. Your private chauffeur will transfer you comfortably to Veer Savarkar International Airport in Port Blair with ample time for your return flight home, carrying sun-kissed memories of emerald island waters and tropical tranquility.

faqs.q: Do Indian citizens need a passport or visa to visit Andaman?
faqs.a: No, Indian citizens do not need a passport or visa. A valid government photo identity card (such as Aadhaar Card, Voter ID, or Driving License) is sufficient for all travel.

faqs.q: Which catamaran ferries are used for island transfers?
faqs.a: We book confirmed luxury air-conditioned catamarans such as Makruzz, Nautika, or Green Ocean with comfortable pushback seats, panoramic sea-view windows, and onboard snack kiosks.

faqs.q: Can non-swimmers try snorkeling and scuba diving?
faqs.a: Yes! Both snorkeling at Elephant Beach and introductory scuba diving are conducted with certified PADI divemasters who hold your hand throughout the experience with full safety gear.

faqs.q: Is Radhanagar Beach safe for swimming?
faqs.a: Yes, Radhanagar Beach has gentle slopes and clean waters, with trained lifeguards stationed during daylight hours, making it one of the safest beaches in Asia for family swimming.

faqs.q: How is mobile network connectivity in the Andaman Islands?
faqs.a: Airtel and BSNL provide reliable 4G connectivity across Port Blair, Havelock, and Neil Island. Resort Wi-Fi is available for essential messaging and browsing.

faqs.q: Are pure vegetarian and Jain meal options available on the islands?
faqs.a: Yes, all our verified partner beachfront resorts feature dedicated vegetarian cooking stations and offer delicious North and South Indian vegetarian meals including Jain preparations.

trips.title: Bali Island Magic (5N/6D)
trips.description: Immerse yourself in the enchanting culture and breathtaking tropical scenery of the Island of the Gods on an authentic Bali holiday. Begin nestled in the lush emerald heart of Ubud, wandering through the ancient stepped rice terraces of Tegalalang, soaring above jungle canopies on the famous Bali jungle swing, and exploring sacred lotus temples and monkey sanctuaries. Continue south to the vibrant coastal beaches of Kuta and Seminyak. Embark on an exhilarating speedboat day excursion to Nusa Penida island to gaze down at the colossal T-Rex shaped coastal cliffs of Kelingking Beach and swim in the natural infinity pool of Angel's Billabong. Marvel at dramatic cliffside Indian Ocean sunsets at Uluwatu Temple, accompanied by the hypnotic chanting and fire choreography of a traditional Kecak dance, capped by a romantic seafood dinner directly on Jimbaran Bay's soft sands. Complete with verified private AC van transfers, dedicated local Balinese guide, handpicked four-star resorts, daily breakfasts and dinners, this flagship Bali tour delivers a truly sublime tropical escape.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Bali & Scenic Transfer to Ubud Rainforest
itinerary.description: Touch down at Ngurah Rai International Airport (DPS) in Denpasar, welcomed by warm tropical breezes and a fragrant frangipani flower garland from your private Balinese guide. Drive north into the cultural heartland of Ubud, winding through traditional craft villages specializing in stone carving, batik textiles, and silver jewelry. Check into your rainforest resort overlooking misty jungle ravines. Settle in with a refreshing tropical welcome mocktail, unwind by the infinity pool, and enjoy an authentic Balinese multi-course dinner featuring fragrant chicken satay and spicy sambal under the stars.

itinerary.title: Tegalalang Rice Terraces, Bali Jungle Swing & Kintamani Volcano
itinerary.description: After an energizing tropical breakfast, journey to the dramatic Tegalalang Rice Terraces, marveling at the ancient subak irrigation engineering that sustains these emerald valley contours. Buckle up for an unforgettable flight on the famous Bali jungle swing high above the canopy. Continue to Kintamani to take in panoramic views of active Mount Batur volcano and its shimmering crater lake. On your return, visit a local coffee plantation to learn the secrets of Luwak coffee brewing, followed by an evening walk through Ubud Art Market before dinner.

itinerary.title: Sacred Monkey Forest, Tegenungan Waterfall & Coastal Transfer
itinerary.description: Begin the morning exploring the ancient sacred banyan trees and moss-covered dragon statues of the Ubud Monkey Forest, home to hundreds of playful long-tailed macaques. Drive south toward the sparkling coastal shores, pausing at Tegenungan Waterfall to feel the cool mountain mist in a lush green gorge. Arrive in the buzzing beachside hub of Kuta/Seminyak, check into your contemporary resort, and enjoy an afternoon lounging on the beach or discovering chic designer boutiques. Enjoy an international buffet dinner at your resort.

itinerary.title: Nusa Penida Island Tour: Kelingking, Broken Beach & Billabong
itinerary.description: Board a morning high-speed boat from Sanur Harbour slicing across the Badung Strait to rugged Nusa Penida island. Drive across dramatic coastal ridges to Kelingking Beach, marveling at the colossal T-Rex shaped cliff plunging into brilliant turquoise waters below. Explore the natural circular limestone arch at Broken Beach and look down into the crystal-clear emerald tide pool of Angel's Billabong. Savor an island lunch, capture unforgettable photos, and board the afternoon speedboat back to the mainland for dinner.

itinerary.title: Tanjung Benoa Water Sports, Uluwatu Cliff Temple & Jimbaran Sunset
itinerary.description: Head to Tanjung Benoa peninsula in the morning for fun coastal watersports including banana boat rides and parasailing. In the late afternoon, drive along the Bukit Peninsula to the dramatic sea cliff of Uluwatu Temple, perched 230 feet above crashing Indian Ocean swells. As the sky turns fiery orange and violet, watch the hypnotic live Kecak fire dance performance narrating the Ramayana epic. Afterward, celebrate your final evening with a candlelit fresh seafood dinner directly on the sandy shores of Jimbaran Bay.

itinerary.title: Bali Souvenir Shopping & Departure Transfer
itinerary.description: Savor your final tropical breakfast by the resort pool, enjoying fresh dragon fruit, mangoes, and Balinese coffee. Take a leisurely morning walk along Seminyak beach or pick up handcrafted souvenirs, handmade aromatic soaps, and Balinese sarongs at Krishna Souvenir Center. Your private chauffeur will assist with luggage and transfer you smoothly to Ngurah Rai International Airport for your flight home, filled with magical memories of Bali.

faqs.q: Do Indian passport holders get Visa on Arrival in Bali?
faqs.a: Yes, Indian passport holders easily obtain a 30-day Visa on Arrival (VoA) at the immigration counters in Denpasar Airport for approx. 500,000 IDR (~₹2,700), payable in cash, card, or USD.

faqs.q: Is the Nusa Penida day trip included in this package?
faqs.a: Yes, return speedboat transfers, entry permits, and a dedicated private vehicle on Nusa Penida to visit Kelingking Beach, Broken Beach, and Angel's Billabong are fully included.

faqs.q: Are vegetarian and Indian meal options available in Bali?
faqs.a: Yes! Bali has an abundance of authentic Indian restaurants (both North and South Indian) as well as pure vegetarian and vegan cafes across Ubud, Seminyak, and Kuta.

faqs.q: What currency should I carry to Bali?
faqs.a: The official currency is the Indonesian Rupiah (IDR). You can carry USD or international multi-currency forex debit cards to withdraw IDR easily from verified bank ATMs across Bali.

faqs.q: Is the famous Bali Jungle Swing safe?
faqs.a: Yes, certified safety harnesses, double tethering ropes, and trained adventure crews supervise every swing at reputable parks like Aloha Ubud and Wanagiri.

faqs.q: Can honeymooners request special room decorations?
faqs.a: Yes! We arrange complimentary honeymoon floral bed decorations and a welcome cake at your partner resorts in Ubud and Seminyak upon prior request at booking.

trips.title: Dazzling Dubai (4N/5D)
trips.description: Immerse yourself in the world's most visionary metropolis on an unforgettable five-day luxury showcase of Dubai and Abu Dhabi. From the moment you land beneath the soaring palm terminals of Dubai International Airport, experience seamless VIP hospitality. Cruise through the Venetian-inspired Dubai Marina on a traditional glass-enclosed wooden Dhow, dining on an international buffet as neon-lit skyscrapers reflect upon the tranquil waters. Ascend at high speed to the 124th and 125th observation decks of the iconic Burj Khalifa, gazing out across the Arabian Gulf, before witnessing the world's largest synchronized water fountains dance to classical melodies. Journey deep into the sweeping crimson dunes of the Lahbab Desert aboard a rugged 4x4 Land Cruiser for heart-pounding dune bashing, camel rides, and an authentic Bedouin camp feast accompanied by Tanura and fire dancers. Expand your horizons with a full-day excursion to Abu Dhabi to witness the marble domes of the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque and the historic BAPS Hindu Mandir.

faqs.q: How long does it take to process a UAE tourist visa for Indian citizens?
faqs.a: UAE tourist e-visas are typically processed within 3 to 4 working days. You simply need to provide clear color passport front and back scans, a passport-sized white background photograph, and confirmed flight details.

faqs.q: What is the dress code for visiting the Sheikh Zayed Grand Mosque in Abu Dhabi?
faqs.a: Modesty is strictly observed. Women must wear loose clothing covering wrists and ankles, and cover their heads with a scarf. Men must wear long trousers and shirts with sleeves. Tight clothing, translucent fabrics, and shorts are strictly forbidden.

faqs.q: Is dune bashing safe for seniors and children?
faqs.a: Dune bashing is thrilling and bumpy. Pregnant women, travellers with back or neck conditions, and infants under 3 years are advised against dune bashing. We can easily arrange for you to travel directly to the campsite in a gentle, non-bashing 4x4 vehicle.

faqs.q: Can I upgrade my Burj Khalifa ticket to the 148th floor (At the Top SKY)?
faqs.a: Yes. Our package includes standard tickets to floors 124 and 125. You can easily upgrade to the VIP 148th floor SKY lounge with priority elevators and refreshments for an additional differential fee.

faqs.q: Is vegetarian, Jain, or Indian food easily available in Dubai?
faqs.a: Dubai is exceptionally welcoming to Indian culinary preferences. Pure vegetarian, Jain, and South/North Indian restaurants are abundant in Bur Dubai, Karama, Deira, and in every major mall food court.

faqs.q: What is the Tourism Dirham fee?
faqs.a: The Tourism Dirham is a nominal mandatory municipal hospitality tax instituted by the Dubai Department of Economy and Tourism. For 4-star hotels, it is AED 15 (approx. ₹340) per bedroom per night, payable directly to the front desk at checkout.

faqs.q: What is the best way to carry money in Dubai?
faqs.a: We recommend carrying a zero-forex-markup card (such as Niyo or bookmyforex) or an international credit card for shopping, along with 200 to 400 AED in cash for small purchases, souk bargains, and tips.

trips.title: Goa Beach Escape (3N/4D)
trips.description: Escape to India's sun-drenched sunshine state for a rejuvenating four-day coastal escape blending sun-bleached Arabian Sea shores with storied Indo-Portuguese heritage. Settle into a tranquil palm-fringed boutique resort in North Goa, where warm tropical ocean breezes set the tone for relaxation. Traverse the historic battlements of 17th-century Fort Aguada and its historic lighthouse overlooking panoramic ocean horizons before delving into the thrill of coastal water sports along Baga and Calangute. Shift pace into cultural discovery as you venture south into the UNESCO World Heritage precinct of Old Goa, marvelling at the gilded baroque altars of the Basilica of Bom Jesus and Se Cathedral. Meander through the vibrant pastel-hued alleys of Fontainhas, Asia's only authentic Latin Quarter, before stepping aboard a sunset catamaran cruise across the Mandovi River with traditional folk rhythms. With private sanitized transfers, daily breakfasts, and curated seaside dining, this trip captures Goa's carefree spirit at its very best.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Goa & Candolim Beach Sunset Leisure
itinerary.description: Arrive at Dabolim Airport (GOI) or Manohar International Airport Mopa (GOX) where your private chauffeur awaits. Enjoy a smooth 45-minute drive past cashew plantations and emerald paddy fields to your beachfront resort in Candolim. Check into your tropical room and unwind by the poolside cabanas with fresh coconut water. In the late afternoon, take a leisurely barefoot stroll along Candolim's golden sand beach as the sky turns fiery crimson over the Arabian Sea. Savor your first authentic Goan coastal dinner at an open-air seaside shack.

itinerary.title: North Goa Coastal Discovery, Fort Aguada & Watersports
itinerary.description: After a lavish buffet breakfast, journey to the dramatic Sinquerim headland to explore 17th-century Fort Aguada and its four-storey stone lighthouse. Gaze out across the endless azure horizon where the Mandovi River meets the open ocean. Next, head to Calangute Beach for a thrilling watersports combo: soar high above the waves while parasailing and skim the surf on a tandem jet-ski. By late afternoon, ascend the ramparts of Chapora Fort for the legendary sunset over Vagator's red cliffs, finishing with music at a hillside lounge.

itinerary.title: Old Goa Heritage Churches, Latin Quarter & Mandovi Cruise
itinerary.description: Delve into Goa's deep spiritual and architectural roots after breakfast. Drive to Old Goa to marvel at the Basilica of Bom Jesus, holding the mortal remains of St. Francis Xavier, and the imposing 16th-century Se Cathedral with its Golden Bell. Continue to the historic Shree Manguesh Temple in Priol before arriving in Panaji. Take a guided heritage walk through Fontainhas, photographing charming Portuguese villas with terracotta roofs and wooden balconies. In the evening, board a scenic Mandovi River sunset cruise featuring live Goan folk dance performances.
activities: Basilica of Bom Jesus Guided Tour

itinerary.title: Local Souvenir Bazaars & Departure Transfer
itinerary.description: Enjoy a slow, sun-dappled morning with breakfast overlooking the swimming pool. Spend your remaining hours shopping for roasted Goan cashews, homemade feni, hand-painted azulejo ceramic tiles, and traditional bebinca sweets at Panaji's vibrant municipal market or Candolim boutique shops. Return to the resort to pack your beachwear and complete checkout formalities. Your private chauffeur will transfer you comfortably to Goa Airport or Madgaon Railway Station for your return journey, refreshed and sun-kissed.

faqs.q: Which airport should I fly into: Dabolim (GOI) or Mopa (GOX)?
faqs.a: Both airports are well-connected. If staying in North Goa (Candolim, Calangute, Baga), Mopa (GOX) is slightly closer (approx. 30-40 minutes drive). Dabolim (GOI) is roughly 50-60 minutes away. Our private transfer service operates seamlessly from both terminals.

faqs.q: Is North Goa or South Goa better for this short break?
faqs.a: North Goa is ideal for a vibrant 4-day trip as it combines lively beaches, water sports, top-rated restaurants, and easy access to Panaji and Old Goa. South Goa is quieter and suited for laid-back luxury stays.

faqs.q: Are water sports included in the package base price?
faqs.a: Watersports (parasailing, jet-skiing, banana boats) are kept as optional direct-payment add-ons so guests who prefer lounging aren't charged unnecessarily. Packages can be pre-upgraded with an adventure pass.

faqs.q: Is the Mandovi River cruise family-friendly?
faqs.a: Yes, absolutely. The Mandovi sunset cruise is a popular family activity featuring live Goan brass bands, Dekhnni folk dances, panoramic river sunset views, and safe double-deck catamarans.

faqs.q: Can we rent self-drive scooters or cars during our stay?
faqs.a: Yes. While our package includes all private sightseeing transfers, our resort reception and concierge can assist you in renting licensed self-drive scooters (approx. ₹400-600/day) with a valid driving license.

faqs.q: What is the dress code for visiting churches in Old Goa?
faqs.a: Visitors must dress respectfully when entering the Basilica of Bom Jesus and Se Cathedral. Sleeveless tops, short skirts, and beachwear are not permitted inside the consecrated sanctuaries.

faqs.q: What local dishes should we not miss in Goa?
faqs.a: Be sure to try authentic Goan fish curry with steamed rice, chicken cafreal, pork vindaloo, freshly baked warm poee bread, and the seven-layered traditional dessert bebinca.

trips.title: Himachal Serenity (6N/7D)
trips.description: Embark on an iconic mountain holiday through Himachal Pradesh, connecting the pine-clad colonial ridges of Shimla with the dramatic alpine valleys of Kullu and Manali. Wander along historic Mall Road in Shimla, pause before the gothic Christ Church on the Ridge, and soak in panoramic Himalayan peaks at Kufri. Journey alongside the turquoise Beas River into Manali, where deodar forests shelter the ancient wooden Hadimba Temple and Old Manali's bohemian cafes. Cross through the architectural marvel of the Atal Tunnel into Lahaul's rugged high-altitude desert, and feel the thrill of paragliding or zorbing across Solang Valley's grassy slopes. Round off your expedition with leisurely shopping and architectural garden walks in planned Chandigarh. Thoughtfully paced with seasoned hill drivers, handpicked four-star valley accommodations, wholesome daily breakfast and dinner, and end-to-end private transfers, this flagship route offers quintessential Himalayan tranquility.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Chandigarh & Scenic Climb to Shimla
itinerary.description: Meet your private chauffeur upon arrival at Chandigarh Airport or Railway Station and set off on the scenic ascending drive toward Shimla. Wind through the lush Shivalik foothills as the air turns refreshingly crisp and fragrant pine forests emerge along the winding highway. Check into your boutique mountain resort overlooking the green valley, refresh yourself with hot tea, and take a gentle sunset stroll along the nearby forested lane. Enjoy a rich North Indian dinner prepared with fresh mountain herbs before resting comfortably.

itinerary.title: Kufri Alpine Excursion & Shimla Colonial Heritage Walk
itinerary.description: After a hearty breakfast, drive to Kufri at 2,630 meters altitude, renowned for its alpine meadows and wide vistas of the snow-clad Greater Himalayas. Explore the Himalayan National Park, capture pictures of native wildlife, and enjoy gentle walks among cedar woods. In the afternoon, return to Shimla for a guided walking tour along the pedestrian-only Mall Road. Admire the neo-gothic Christ Church on the Ridge, browse the bustling Lakkar Bazaar for wooden handicrafts, and savor evening treats at heritage bakeries before dinner.

itinerary.title: Shimla to Manali Valley via Pandoh Dam & Kullu
itinerary.description: Depart early following a wholesome breakfast for the picturesque journey toward Manali. Follow the twisting canyon road as it snakes past Sundernagar Lake and the turquoise reservoir of Pandoh Dam. Continue through the orchard-strewn Kullu Valley running parallel to the roaring Beas River, stopping at an authentic Kullu shawl weaving cooperative and local apple orchard. Arrive in Manali by late afternoon, check in to your riverside valley resort, and listen to the relaxing rush of mountain water under star-studded alpine skies.

itinerary.title: Ancient Hadimba Temple, Vashisht Springs & Old Manali
itinerary.description: Begin the morning exploring the ancient four-tiered pagoda Hadimba Temple, nestled deep within centuries-old giant deodar cedar trees. Cross the river to visit the sacred sage Vashisht temple complex, famous for its natural therapeutic sulfur hot springs where you can dip your feet. Spend the afternoon wandering through the vibrant cobblestone lanes of Old Manali, browsing indie artisan shops, tasting artisan trout, and visiting the peaceful Tibetan Buddhist monastery. Return to your lodge for evening campfire and a delicious buffet dinner.

itinerary.title: Solang Valley Adventures & Atal Tunnel Crossing
itinerary.description: Dedicate today to heart-pumping alpine adventures in the renowned Solang Valley. Depending on the season, partake in paragliding with panoramic views of Pir Panjal peaks, zorbing across lush grassy meadows, or winter snow sledding. Afterwards, continue north through the engineering marvel of the 9.02-kilometer Atal Tunnel, emerging on the North Portal to witness the stark, majestic mountain scenery of Sissu in Lahaul Valley. Return to Manali in the late afternoon for relaxed shopping along the Mall Road before your farewell mountain dinner.

itinerary.title: Manali to Chandigarh via Mandi & Bilaspur
itinerary.description: Savor your final mountain breakfast overlooking pine ridges before starting the gradual descent back toward the plains of Chandigarh. Trace the Beas River down the Kullu gorge, passing through historic Mandi and terraced farmland. Stop for fresh roadside refreshments and fruit preserves along the route. Arrive in the evening at your contemporary hotel in Chandigarh, unwind from the journey, and enjoy a comfortable dinner showcasing authentic Punjabi cuisine.

itinerary.title: Chandigarh Rock Garden, Sukhna Lake & Departure
itinerary.description: After breakfast, check out and embark on a morning tour of Chandigarh's most celebrated landmarks. Marvel at the visionary recycled sculptures of Nek Chand at the iconic Rock Garden, and enjoy a serene lakeside walk beside the placid waters of Sukhna Lake against the backdrop of the Shivalik hills. Later, your chauffeur will transfer you to Chandigarh Airport or Railway Station in good time for your onward journey home with cherished Himalayan memories.

faqs.q: What is the best time to visit Shimla and Manali?
faqs.a: March to June offers pleasant weather for sightseeing and outdoor adventures. December to February is ideal for travelers seeking heavy snowfall, skiing, and winter landscapes.

faqs.q: Is crossing the Atal Tunnel included in this itinerary?
faqs.a: Yes, the itinerary includes a scenic drive through the 9-kilometer Atal Tunnel to witness the dramatic landscape shift into the Lahaul Valley at Sissu, subject to weather conditions.

faqs.q: Can Rohtang Pass be visited on this tour?
faqs.a: Rohtang Pass permits are regulated by the National Green Tribunal and operate via local union taxis from May to October. We can easily arrange permits and union vehicles upon request.

faqs.q: What vehicle is provided for mountain travel?
faqs.a: We provide sanitized, private AC sedans (Dzire/Etios) for couples and comfortable Toyota Innova Crysta SUVs for families, steered by seasoned mountain-certified chauffeurs.

faqs.q: Is river rafting in Kullu safe for beginners?
faqs.a: Yes, commercial river rafting on the Beas River in Kullu is overseen by licensed river guides with compulsory life jackets and safety gear, suitable for beginners and families.

faqs.q: Are vegetarian and Jain meals available at the hotels?
faqs.a: Yes, all our handpicked partner resorts provide extensive pure vegetarian and Jain food selections upon prior request at the time of booking.

trips.title: Iceland Aurora & Glaciers (6N/7D)
trips.description: Journey to the edge of the Arctic Circle on an extraordinary expedition across the Land of Fire and Ice. Begin in the colorful Nordic capital of Reykjavik before heading into the wild volcanic landscapes of Iceland's famed Golden Circle. Stand in awe as the Strokkur geyser hurls steaming boiling water into the crisp polar sky, marvel at the two-tiered torrents of Gullfoss waterfall, and walk the continental rift valley between North American and Eurasian tectonic plates at Thingvellir National Park. Venture along the dramatic southern coastline, strolling behind the roaring curtain of Seljalandsfoss waterfall and walking beneath towering basalt sea stacks along the brooding volcanic sands of Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach. Watch colossal turquoise icebergs drift out to the Atlantic at Jokulsarlon Glacier Lagoon and glitter on Diamond Beach. By night, chase the ethereal emerald ribbons of the Aurora Borealis under dark Nordic skies, and soak away in the mineral-rich milky geothermal waters of the world-famous Blue Lagoon.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Reykjavik & Nordic Capital Harbor Walk
itinerary.description: Touch down at Keflavik International Airport (KEF), greeted by the fresh sub-arctic air of Iceland. Board your premium heated private transport and drive across the otherworldly moss-covered lava fields of the Reykjanes peninsula into Reykjavik. Check into your contemporary 4-star hotel in the city center. Take a relaxed evening stroll along Laugavegur shopping street, admire the striking modern architecture of Harpa Concert Hall reflecting the harbor waters, and gaze up at the towering spire of Hallgrimskirkja church. Savor a comforting dinner featuring fresh Nordic salmon and warm root vegetables.

itinerary.title: The Golden Circle: Thingvellir, Geysir & Thundering Gullfoss
itinerary.description: Embark on Iceland's most famous scenic route, the Golden Circle. First, explore Thingvellir National Park, where the North American and Eurasian tectonic plates are actively pulling apart, leaving dramatic canyon walkways where the world's oldest parliament met in 930 AD. Continue to the Haukadalur geothermal valley to watch the Strokkur geyser reliably erupt every 6 to 10 minutes, shooting boiling columns 30 meters high. Next, marvel at Gullfoss (Golden Falls) as glacier-fed waters plummet down two massive rocky steps into a rugged canyon. Return to Reykjavik for dinner.

itinerary.title: South Coast Waterfalls, Seljalandsfoss & Skogafoss
itinerary.description: Travel east along Iceland's scenic Ring Road, hugged by dramatic sea cliffs and distant snow-covered volcanoes. Pause at Seljalandsfoss, one of the world's rare waterfalls where a secure footpath allows you to walk completely behind the thundering water curtain. Continue to the mighty 60-meter drop of Skogafoss, often crowned with vivid double rainbows in the mist. Visit the nearby Skogar Folk Museum to see traditional turf-roofed farmhouses. Arrive by late afternoon in the coastal village of Vik, check into your boutique hotel, and prepare for night aurora monitoring.

itinerary.title: Reynisfjara Black Sand Beach & Jokulsarlon Glacier Lagoon
itinerary.description: Spend the morning walking across the jet-black volcanic sands of Reynisfjara Beach, marveling at the colossal hexagonal basalt sea columns and the roaring Atlantic breakers against Reynisdrangar sea stacks. Drive east beneath the massive Vatnajokull ice cap to the breathtaking Jokulsarlon Glacier Lagoon. Watch enormous luminescent blue icebergs calved from the glacier drift slowly toward the sea. Cross the road to Diamond Beach, where sculpted clear ice blocks wash ashore and sparkle like giant diamonds on the pitch-black sand. Return to Vik for dinner.

itinerary.title: Lava Fields of Eldhraun, Kerid Crater & Night Aurora Chase
itinerary.description: Journey through Eldhraun, the world's largest moss-draped volcanic lava field, created during the catastrophic 1783 Laki eruption. Stop at the dramatic Kerid volcanic crater, gazing down at its vibrant aquamarine mineral lake nestled inside deep crimson volcanic rock walls. Continue to your riverside hotel in Selfoss. After dinner, set out on a dedicated guided Northern Lights hunting excursion into dark, cloud-free valleys far from city lights. Watch in silent wonder as luminous green and violet auroral curtains ripple across the Arctic night sky.

itinerary.title: Geothermal Wonders & Blue Lagoon Thermal Spa Experience
itinerary.description: After breakfast, drive west across the boiling geothermal vents and rugged black hills of the Reykjanes peninsula. Arrive at the world-renowned Blue Lagoon geothermal spa. Slip into the 38°C to 40°C mineral-rich milky blue waters, naturally heated by subterranean volcanic aquifers and infused with skin-nourishing silica and algae. Apply a therapeutic silica mud mask from the in-water bar and relax with a refreshing beverage while steam drifts across black volcanic lava rocks. Transfer to your airport hotel for a celebratory farewell dinner.

itinerary.title: Keflavik Airport Departure & Memories of Fire and Ice
itinerary.description: Savor your final Nordic breakfast with artisan rye breads, smoked salmon, and hot skyr. Take a morning breath of the crisp sub-arctic sea air before your chauffeur transfers you directly to Keflavik International Airport (KEF). Check in for your flight home, gazing down over the glaciers, fjords, and volcanic peaks of Iceland as you soar homeward with extraordinary memories of northern magic.

faqs.q: When is the best time to see the Northern Lights in Iceland?
faqs.a: September through March offers the darkest skies and highest probability of solar auroral activity. Our expert guides track cloud coverage and solar storms to position you in prime dark sky spots.

faqs.q: Is admission to the Blue Lagoon included in the package?
faqs.a: Yes, Comfort Admission to the Blue Lagoon is fully included, providing a complimentary beverage from the swim-up bar, a silica mud face mask, and towel rental.

faqs.q: Do Indian passport holders require a visa for Iceland?
faqs.a: Yes, a valid Schengen Tourist Visa is required. Our visa support team assists with verified hotel confirmations, detailed itineraries, and application document checklists.

faqs.q: Can vegetarian and Indian meals be arranged in Iceland?
faqs.a: Yes! Reykjavik and coastal towns feature excellent Indian and vegetarian dining establishments. Our partner hotels also provide hearty vegetarian pasta, soups, and vegetable risottos.

faqs.q: How cold does it get in Iceland during winter?
faqs.a: Due to the warming North Atlantic Gulf Stream, coastal winter temperatures in Iceland typically hover around -2°C to +4°C, which is warmer than winter in New York or Chicago, though windproof clothing is essential.

faqs.q: Are credit cards widely accepted across Iceland?
faqs.a: Iceland is virtually a cashless society. International Visa and Mastercard credit and debit cards with chip and PIN are accepted everywhere, even at rural restrooms and roadside cafes.

trips.title: Classic Japan (6N/7D)
trips.description: Experience the magical harmony of ancient traditions and futuristic marvels with infiYATRA's 7-day Classic Japan Golden Route expedition. Your voyage commences amidst the neon skyscapes and bustling crosswalks of Tokyo, where century-old Senso-ji Temple rubs shoulders with vibrant Harajuku youth culture and cutting-edge digital art installations at teamLab Planets. Ascend into the peaceful mountain atmosphere of Hakone for postcard-perfect vistas of sacred Mount Fuji, taking an exhilarating ride on the Hakone Komagatake Ropeway and relaxing in therapeutic natural volcanic onsens followed by an authentic multi-course Kaiseki dinner. Board the lightning-fast Shinkansen bullet train hurtling across Honshu to Kyoto, the historic heart of Japan. Wander through thousands of vermilion torii gates at Fushimi Inari Taisha, listen to rustling green stalks in the ethereal Arashiyama Bamboo Grove, admire the glimmering gold pavilion of Kinkaku-ji, and stroll through lantern-lit alleyways of Gion seeking glimpses of graceful Geishas. With 4-star handpicked accommodations, dedicated English-speaking local guides, and seamless transport arrangements, Japan's finest wonders unfold effortlessly.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Tokyo | Welcome to Shinjuku
itinerary.description: Touch down at Tokyo Haneda or Narita International Airport where an infiYATRA airport representative welcomes you and escorts you via private airport transfer to your upscale hotel in Shinjuku. After settling in and freshening up, take your first evening stroll into the bustling Shinjuku district. Marvel at the kaleidoscopic glow of digital billboards, wander past the legendary Godzilla head, and sample your first steaming bowls of artisanal ramen or crispy gyoza at local izakayas before resting up for an exhilarating adventure.

itinerary.title: Tokyo Metropolis: Senso-ji, Shibuya Crossing & Harajuku
itinerary.description: Begin your exploration with a hearty breakfast before meeting your guide for a full-day Tokyo immersion. Visit Senso-ji, Tokyo's oldest Buddhist temple in historic Asakusa, browsing lively Nakamise shopping street for traditional souvenirs and matcha treats. Next, immerse yourself in youth trends along Harajuku’s Takeshita Street before finding quiet serenity beneath the towering camphor trees of Meiji Jingu Shrine. Conclude your afternoon navigating the famous scramble crossing at Shibuya and snapping photos with the bronze statue of faithful Hachiko.

itinerary.title: TeamLab Planets, Akihabara & Tokyo Bay Cruise
itinerary.description: Step into the future today with pre-booked morning admission to teamLab Planets in Toyosu, where you walk barefoot through immersive interactive digital water and blooming light crystal exhibits. Afterwards, head over to Akihabara Electric Town to discover multi-level electronics plazas and anime collectibles. Later in the afternoon, embark on a relaxing Tokyo Bay sightseeing cruise from Hinode Pier to Odaiba, admiring the illuminated Rainbow Bridge and miniature Statue of Liberty before enjoying dinner overlooking the bay waterfront.

itinerary.title: Hakone & Mount Fuji Scenic Excursion & Onsen Kaiseki
itinerary.description: Bid farewell to Tokyo as your private transfer heads toward picturesque Hakone National Park at the foot of Mount Fuji. Embark on a pirate ship cruise across shimmering Lake Ashi offering breathtaking views of sacred Fuji reflected on calm waters. Board the Hakone Ropeway gliding above smoking sulfuric vents of Owakudani volcanic valley, where you can taste boiled black eggs reputed to prolong longevity. Check into your traditional onsen resort, soak in mineral hot springs, and savor an authentic Kaiseki banquet dinner.

itinerary.title: Shinkansen Bullet Train to Kyoto & Gion Geisha District
itinerary.description: Following breakfast, transfer to Odawara Station to board the sleek Shinkansen bullet train racing along the Pacific coastline to cultural Kyoto at speeds exceeding 285 km/h. Arrive in Kyoto by noon and check into your centrally located hotel. In the late afternoon, join a walking tour through historic Gion, Kyoto's premier geisha quarter. Amble down preserved wooden Machiya shopfronts of Hanami-koji Lane and Shirakawa canal, soaking in the timeless atmosphere as paper lanterns flicker to life at dusk.

itinerary.title: Kyoto Shrines & Arashiyama Bamboo Grove
itinerary.description: Embark on an enchanting full-day tour of Kyoto’s most treasured UNESCO World Heritage sites. Start early at Fushimi Inari Taisha, hiking through thousands of bright vermilion torii gates winding up the sacred forested mountain. Continue to western Kyoto to step inside the mesmerizing Arashiyama Bamboo Grove and cross the historic Togetsukyo Bridge. Conclude your journey admiring Kinkaku-ji, the Golden Pavilion whose top two floors are covered in pure gold leaf shimmering over a tranquil mirror pond.

itinerary.title: Kyoto to Osaka Departure | Sayonara Japan
itinerary.description: Savor your final Japanese breakfast at the hotel and spend your morning gathering handcrafted souvenirs, green tea delicacies, and ceramics in downtown Kyoto or Nishiki Market. At the scheduled time, our private transfer picks you up from the hotel lobby and drives you smoothly to Osaka Kansai International Airport (KIX) or Tokyo Haneda for your return flight back to India, carrying unforgettable memories of the Land of the Rising Sun with infiYATRA.

faqs.q: What is the best season to book this Japan Golden Route tour?
faqs.a: Spring (late March to mid-April) is famed for cherry blossoms (Sakura), while autumn (October to November) offers glorious vibrant fall foliage and crisp clear skies with the best Fuji visibility. Both seasons are prime times to travel.

faqs.q: Do Indian passport holders require a tourist visa for Japan?
faqs.a: Yes, Indian citizens require a valid Japan tourist visa prior to departure. infiYATRA assists with full documentation guidance, hotel booking vouchers, and itinerary cover letters for submission to the VFS Japan application center.

faqs.q: Is luggage forwarding available between Tokyo and Kyoto?
faqs.a: Yes! Japan's luggage courier service (Takkyubin) is world-renowned. For overnight stays in Hakone, you can conveniently ship your large suitcase directly to Kyoto for approx. 2,000 JPY, traveling light with an overnight bag.

faqs.q: Are vegetarian and Indian food options readily available in Japan?
faqs.a: Yes, major cities like Tokyo and Kyoto have numerous authentic Indian restaurants. Furthermore, our guides help you navigate vegetarian-friendly Japanese ramen, soba, tempura, and convenience store favorites.

faqs.q: What are the rules for enjoying the traditional onsen hot springs in Hakone?
faqs.a: Traditional Japanese onsens are gender-separated and entered without clothing after thoroughly washing at the shower stations. Guests with small tattoos can be provided waterproof covers or book private family onsens.

faqs.q: How fast does the Shinkansen bullet train travel?
faqs.a: The Tokaido Shinkansen bullet train operates at operational speeds up to 285 km/h, delivering an ultra-smooth, punctually timed, and scenic journey between the Tokyo region and Kyoto in just over two hours.

trips.tagline: Bullet trains across Honshu, glowing Shinjuku skyscapes, sacred Mount Fuji in Hakone, and thousand-torii gates of Kyoto.

bestTime.notes: Spring (late March to mid-April) brings blooming pink Sakura cherry blossoms; Autumn (October to November) features vibrant crimson Japanese maples and crystal-clear skies for Mount Fuji views.

trips.title: Kashmir Paradise (6N/7D)
trips.description: Surrender to the timeless grandeur of Kashmir on this handcrafted seven-day voyage through India's fabled northern jewel. Your journey begins upon the tranquil mirror of Dal Lake, drifting in a hand-carved cedar houseboat adorned with walnut carvings and fragrant Kashmiri deodar woods. Glide under the golden dusk on a cushioned private Shikara before travelling south through saffron-scented Pampore fields to Pahalgam's whispering pine valleys. Here along the rushing Lidder River, discover Betaab Valley's alpine pastures and the pristine snowmelt waters of Aru. Next, ascend to alpine heights at Gulmarg, riding the legendary Kongdoori Gondola cable car toward snow-capped Apharwat Peak. Complete your Himalayan circle in historic Srinagar with walks through centuries-old terraced Mughal gardens, vibrant old-quarter spice bazaars, and an exhilarating day excursion to the Thajiwas Glacier in Sonmarg. Balanced with private heated transport, handpicked mountain resorts, and daily authentic meals, this is Kashmir experienced with poise, safety, and heartfelt hospitality.

Sunset private Shikara cruise gliding past floating gardens and wooden footbridges

itinerary.title: Arrival in Srinagar & Dal Lake Sunset Shikara
itinerary.description: Touch down at Srinagar Airport where your private expedition host greets you warmly with fragrant Kashmiri Kahwa. Transfer 15 kilometers through Chinar-lined avenues to the Dal Lake jetty. Board a wooden Shikara to reach your hand-carved heritage houseboat. After settling into your cedarwood suite, embark on a sunset Shikara ride across the lotus-dappled waters. Glide past floating flower bazaars, Char Chinar island, and heritage wooden houseboats framed by the Zabarwan mountain range before enjoying a traditional multi-course dinner on board.

itinerary.title: Srinagar to Pahalgam via Saffron Fields & Avantipura
itinerary.description: Savor breakfast overlooking the misty lake before checking out for your scenic 90-kilometer drive south to Pahalgam, the Valley of Shepherds. En route, pause at the purple-tinged saffron fields of Pampore to sample organic saffron threads and local dry fruits. Continue past the 9th-century stone carvings of the Avantipura ruins dedicated to Lord Vishnu. By afternoon, ascend into the whispering pine forests flanking the turquoise Lidder River. Check into your riverfront resort and spend a tranquil evening strolling along the pebble riverbanks.

itinerary.title: Valleys of Pahalgam: Betaab Valley, Aru & Chandanwari
itinerary.description: Awake to birdsong and mountain vistas. Board authorized local union vehicles for a comprehensive valley tour. First explore Betaab Valley, named after the Bollywood classic, with its lush meadows ringed by snow-draped deodars and crystal streams. Next, wind upward 12 kilometers to Aru Valley, an idyllic eco-village where quiet shepherds tend grazing flocks amidst wildflower meadows. In the afternoon, visit Chandanwari, the historical gateway to the holy Amarnath Yatra pilgrimage, before returning to Pahalgam town for steaming Rogan Josh and evening shopping.

itinerary.title: Pahalgam to Gulmarg Meadow of Flowers
itinerary.description: Depart Pahalgam after breakfast on a scenic 140-kilometer drive across the Kashmir valley floor toward the Pir Panjal range. Wind up the forested slopes of Tangmarg where firs tower overhead. By early afternoon, arrive in Gulmarg, perched at 8,690 feet above sea level. Check into your cozy alpine lodge. Spend your afternoon wandering the sprawling green golf course meadows, visiting the heritage wooden St. Mary's Church built during the British era, or simply savoring warm walnut tarts at a traditional hillside cafe.

itinerary.title: Gulmarg Gondola Ride & Return to Srinagar
itinerary.description: After an early breakfast, proceed to the Gulmarg Gondola station, one of the highest operating cable cars on earth. Board your enclosed six-seater cabin for the thrilling Phase 1 ascent to Kongdoori mountain bowl at 10,000 feet. Gaze in awe at panoramic snow fields, glacial cirques, and distant Nanga Parbat on clear days. Spend the morning walking amidst alpine snow. In the afternoon, descend to the base and drive 55 kilometers back to Srinagar. Check into your luxury city hotel for a relaxed evening.

itinerary.title: Day Excursion to Sonmarg Meadow of Gold & Thajiwas Glacier
itinerary.description: Set out on an exhilarating morning excursion to Sonmarg, Meadow of Gold, situated 85 kilometers northeast of Srinagar along the roaring Sindh River. Drive through dramatic gorges, walnut groves, and alpine forests with towering granite peaks. Upon arrival in Sonmarg at 9,000 feet, embark on a pony trek or scenic alpine walk to the foot of Thajiwas Glacier. Touch eternal summer snowfields and watch silver waterfalls cascade down glacial moraines. Return to Srinagar by evening for farewell shopping at the Polo View craft market.

itinerary.title: Mughal Terraced Gardens & Airport Farewell
itinerary.description: Conclude your Himalayan sojourn with a morning cultural tour of Srinagar's crown jewels. Walk through Nishat Bagh (Garden of Bliss) built in 1633, with its twelve terraced stone cascades framed by majestic Chinar trees. Next, explore Shalimar Bagh, the romantic garden built by Emperor Jahangir for Queen Nur Jahan. After a farewell sip of saffron tea and last-minute procurement of pure pashmina or walnuts, transfer to Srinagar International Airport for your departure flight, enriched with golden memories of paradise.

faqs.q: Is Kashmir safe for families and solo female travellers?
faqs.a: Yes, absolutely. Tourism is the heartbeat of Kashmir. Thousands of families and couples visit year-round. Tour operators, hotel staff, and shikara owners extend extraordinary warmth and hospitality. We provide verified local chauffeurs and 24/7 concierge assistance.

faqs.q: Why don't outside cabs go to Betaab and Aru Valley in Pahalgam?
faqs.a: Per local district administration and taxi union regulations, outside tourist vehicles are permitted only up to the hotel in Pahalgam. Exploring internal spots like Betaab Valley, Aru, and Chandanwari requires local registered union cabs, which are already included in our package.

faqs.q: Are Gulmarg Gondola Phase 1 tickets guaranteed?
faqs.a: We book your Phase 1 Gondola tickets through the JKCCC portal as soon as your booking is confirmed. However, operations remain subject to daily mountain weather and wind safety protocols determined by the cable car authority.

faqs.q: What is the best time to experience snow in Gulmarg?
faqs.a: For fresh snow and skiing, mid-December through March is ideal. For pleasant spring meadows, blooming flowers, and cool weather, April through June offers the most comfortable temperatures.

faqs.q: Will my mobile phone work in Srinagar, Gulmarg, and Pahalgam?
faqs.a: Only Indian postpaid connections (Airtel, Jio, and BSNL) function in Jammu & Kashmir. Prepaid SIM cards purchased outside J&K will stop receiving network signals upon crossing into the state due to national security regulations.

faqs.q: What is the difference between Dal Lake and Nigeen Lake houseboats?
faqs.a: Dal Lake houseboats offer lively vistas with vibrant floating markets, Shikara traffic, and panoramic Zabarwan mountain views. Nigeen Lake is slightly calmer and quieter. Our standard package includes premier category Dal Lake houseboats.

faqs.q: What traditional food should I try during the trip?
faqs.a: Do not miss the traditional Kashmiri Wazwan feast featuring Rogan Josh, Rista (meatballs in saffron gravy), Gushtaba, and vegetarian specialties like Nadru Yakhni (lotus stem in yogurt) and Dum Aloo, accompanied by hot walnut chutney.

trips.description: Immerse your senses in the verdant paradise of Kerala on this handcrafted seven-day journey across the Western Ghats and palm-sheltered Arabian backwaters. Begin amidst the colonial history of Fort Kochi, watching cantilevered Chinese fishing nets dip into the sunset tide. Journey upward through winding cloud-kissed mountain roads to Munnar, where endless rolling carpeted tea hills stretch toward Anamudi peak. Track the endangered Nilgiri Tahr along the cliff paths of Eravikulam National Park and savor fresh single-estate brew at the historic Tata Tea Museum. Wind through cardamom, cinnamon, and pepper hills to Thekkady for an aromatic spice plantation walk and live Kalaripayattu martial arts display. The journey reaches its serene zenith as you step onto your private traditional thatch-roofed Kettuvallam houseboat in Alleppey, gliding along Vembanad Lake canals while feasting on fresh Karimeen fish and Malabar curries. Complete with verified chauffeur transfers, boutique nature resorts, and daily breakfasts, this is Kerala at its most enchanting.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Cochin & Fort Kochi Colonial Heritage
itinerary.description: Arrive at Cochin International Airport (COK) where your private chauffeur welcomes you. Transfer 42 kilometers across backwater bridges to your heritage hotel in historic Fort Kochi. After checking in and freshening up, take a guided afternoon stroll along the waterfront promenade. Watch the iconic 14th-century Chinese fishing nets swing into the Arabian Sea against the golden sunset. Visit St. Francis Church, the oldest European church in India where Vasco da Gama was initially buried, and browse antique curiosities along Jew Street.

itinerary.title: Cochin to Munnar via Cheeyappara & Valara Waterfalls
itinerary.description: After a hearty South Indian breakfast, depart Cochin for the four-hour ascent into the misty Western Ghats heading toward Munnar. Watch the coastal plains give way to cascading rubber estates, pineapple groves, and deep forested mountain ravines. En route, pause at the tiered Cheeyappara Waterfalls tumbling down seven rocky tiers, followed by the lush gorge of Valara Falls. Arrive at Munnar (5,200 ft) by early afternoon. Check into your mountain resort perched above misty tea valleys and spend the evening enjoying crisp mountain breezes.

itinerary.title: Munnar Tea Plantations, Eravikulam & Mattupetty Dam
itinerary.description: Wake to morning mist swirling across the tea valleys. Travel by department eco-bus into Eravikulam National Park, home to the largest surviving population of the endangered Nilgiri Tahr mountain goat. Hike along gentle paved trails offering sweeping views of Anamudi, South India's highest peak. In the afternoon, visit the historic Tata Tea Museum to witness century-old orthodox tea rolling machinery and sample fresh golden Pekoe. Continue to scenic Mattupetty Dam and Echo Point before returning to the resort for an evening bonfire.

itinerary.title: Munnar to Thekkady: Spice Plantations & Cultural Evening
itinerary.description: Check out after breakfast and drive south through the Cardamom Hills to Thekkady, the spice capital of Kerala adjoining Periyar Tiger Reserve. The scenic 90-kilometer drive winds past rubber and coffee plantations. Arrive and check into your eco-lodge surrounded by towering trees. In the afternoon, embark on an aromatic guided walking tour through an organic spice plantation to touch and smell growing pepper vines, green cardamom, cinnamon bark, and nutmeg. In the evening, witness an enthralling live performance of Kalaripayattu martial arts.

itinerary.title: Thekkady Wildlife & Alleppey Backwaters Houseboat Cruise
itinerary.description: Take an optional early morning boat safari on Periyar Lake inside the sanctuary before descending from the hills toward the coastal backwaters of Alleppey. Arrive at the private jetty by noon and board your traditional thatch-roofed Kettuvallam houseboat. As the captain navigates into the palm-canopied canals of Vembanad Lake, savor a fresh lunch of Karimeen Pollichathu and piping hot red rice prepared by your private onboard chef. Drift past duck farming hamlets, coir-weaving village docks, and water lilies before anchoring for a tranquil starlit dinner.

itinerary.title: Alleppey Backwaters to Cochin & Jew Town History
itinerary.description: Savor morning tea on the open sundeck as the sun rises over water lilies and village canoes glide past. Enjoy a freshly prepared breakfast of soft appams and vegetable stew before disembarking at 9:30 AM. Drive 55 kilometers north along the coastal highway to Cochin. Check into your luxury city hotel. Spend the afternoon exploring Mattancherry Palace with its exquisite 16th-century Hindu mythological murals, followed by the Paradesi Jewish Synagogue with its hand-painted blue Cantonese porcelain tiles and historic clock tower.

itinerary.title: Lulu Mall Souvenirs & Airport Departure
itinerary.description: Enjoy a relaxed breakfast at your hotel. Spend your morning picking up authentic banana chips fried in pure coconut oil, Kasavu handloom sarees, aromatic tea packs, and Malabar spices at Cochin's vibrant markets or the grand Lulu Mall. Return to the hotel for checkout. Your chauffeur will provide a punctual transfer to Cochin International Airport (COK) or Ernakulam Railway Station for your onward journey, leaving you deeply rejuvenated by the beauty and warmth of God's Own Country.

faqs.q: Is the Alleppey houseboat private for our family or shared?
faqs.a: Our packages feature an exclusive, fully private houseboat for your travelling party. You will have a dedicated captain, navigator, and private chef on board catering solely to your preferences.

faqs.q: What is the food like on board the houseboat?
faqs.a: Meals are freshly prepared on board using local ingredients. Typical lunch includes traditional Kerala rice, sambar, thoran, avial, and freshly caught Karimeen fish fry. Vegetarian, Jain, and North Indian meal choices are gladly accommodated on request.

faqs.q: How cold does it get in Munnar?
faqs.a: Munnar sits at an altitude of 5,200 feet. Daytime temperatures range from 18°C to 24°C, while nighttime temperatures can dip to 10°C to 14°C between November and February. A light fleece jacket or shawl is recommended.

faqs.q: Can elderly travellers and young children comfortably do this circuit?
faqs.a: Yes. This circuit is one of India's most popular family routes with well-paved highways, gentle walks, and relaxing boat experiences. Vehicles stop at scenic viewpoints to break up hill driving.

faqs.q: Are vegetarian and Jain food easily available in Kerala?
faqs.a: Yes, Kerala boasts one of India's richest vegetarian culinary traditions with dishes like Sadya, vegetable stew with appams, and dosas. All partner hotels and the houseboat chef gladly prepare pure vegetarian and Jain meals without onion or garlic upon prior notice.

faqs.q: What spices are best to buy in Thekkady?
faqs.a: Thekkady is world-famous for fresh green cardamom, Tellicherry black peppercorns, whole cinnamon bark, cloves, nutmeg, and organic vanilla pods. We take you to authorized cooperative government-approved spice gardens.

faqs.q: What is Kalaripayattu?
faqs.a: Kalaripayattu is one of the oldest fighting martial arts systems on earth, originating in Kerala over 3,000 years ago. The live 1-hour evening performance showcases incredible agility, flexibility, sword duels, and fire acrobatics.

trips.title: Leh Ladakh Odyssey (6N/7D)
trips.description: Embark on an unforgettable high-altitude expedition across Ladakh, the Land of High Passes, where dramatic lunar valleys meet azure glacial lakes beneath the rooftop of the world. Begin in Leh with essential acclimatization, discovering the sacred halls of Thiksey Monastery, the cliffside historic Leh Palace, and the gravity-defying marvel of Magnetic Hill. Ascend through the legendary Khardung La at 17,982 feet into the fertile oasis of Nubra Valley. Ride double-humped Bactrian camels across the silver sand dunes of Hunder against a backdrop of snow-capped peaks, and visit the serene 106-foot golden Maitreya Buddha at Diskit Monastery. Traverse the rugged Shyok canyon route to reach the ethereal, color-shifting waters of Pangong Tso Lake at 14,270 feet, spending a starlit night in luxury insulated lakeside camps. Steered by certified high-altitude mountain drivers in 4x4 vehicles with onboard medical oxygen, heated rooms, and warm meals, this expedition promises the ultimate Himalayan journey.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Leh & Crucial High-Altitude Acclimatization
itinerary.description: Touch down at Kushok Bakula Rimpochee Airport in Leh at 11,500 feet altitude, surrounded by dramatic barren peaks. Meet your local Ladakhi escort and transfer to your hotel. Strict complete rest is mandatory for the remainder of the day to allow your body to comfortably acclimatize to the thin mountain air. Drink plenty of warm water, ginger-lemon tea, and garlic soup. In the evening, take a gentle stroll around Leh Market or admire the illuminated white dome of Shanti Stupa in the distance before an early dinner.

itinerary.title: Sham Valley: Hall of Fame, Magnetic Hill & Sangam Confluence
itinerary.description: After a hearty breakfast, set out along the picturesque Leh-Srinagar highway to explore the cultural landmarks of Sham Valley. Pay homage to brave soldiers at the Indian Army Hall of Fame museum. Experience the gravity-defying optical phenomenon at Magnetic Hill, where vehicles appear to roll uphill in neutral. Stop at Gurudwara Pathar Sahib, maintained by army regiments. Continue to the dramatic confluence of the muddy Indus River and turquoise Zanskar River at Nimmu. Return to Leh in the late afternoon to visit the Shanti Stupa for sunset over the Zanskar range.

itinerary.title: Leh to Nubra Valley via Majestic Khardung La Pass
itinerary.description: Depart early after breakfast for an exhilarating mountain drive over Khardung La, one of the highest motorable mountain passes on Earth at 17,982 feet. Pause at the summit prayer flags for triumphant photos of the snow-clad Karakoram Range before descending into the fertile Nubra Valley, historically part of the ancient Silk Route. Arrive at Diskit to witness the magnificent 106-foot statue of Maitreya Buddha perched over the valley. Continue to Hunder village, check into your luxury valley resort, and relax among apricot trees.

itinerary.title: Hunder White Sand Dunes & Turtuk Border Village Excursion
itinerary.description: Begin the day riding rare double-humped Bactrian camels across the silver sand dunes of Hunder, a surreal desert landscape nestled against icy peaks. Afterward, drive alongside the turquoise Shyok River to Turtuk, India's northernmost village near the Line of Control, opened to tourists only in 2010. Explore stone-paved lanes, apricot orchards, and the historic palace of the Yabgo royal dynasty in this unique Balti Muslim enclave. Taste fresh dried apricots and walnut chutney before returning to your Nubra resort for dinner under a brilliant canopy of stars.

itinerary.title: Nubra Valley to Pangong Tso Lake via Shyok River Canyon
itinerary.description: After breakfast, depart Hunder along the rugged, dramatic canyon road of the Shyok River route directly connecting Nubra to Pangong Tso. As you climb the final ridge, the breathless sight of Pangong Tso opens up—a 134-kilometer-long lake extending into Tibet, shifting between shades of deep sapphire, cerulean, and emerald green under changing sunlight. Check into your deluxe lakeside camp at 14,270 feet. Walk along the tranquil shore, watch the sunset paint the barren mountains in violet and amber, and stargaze into the Milky Way after dinner.

itinerary.title: Pangong Sunrise to Leh via Chang La Pass & Thiksey Monastery
itinerary.description: Wake early to witness a magical Himalayan sunrise reflecting across the glassy waters of Pangong Tso. After a warm breakfast, begin the return journey to Leh crossing the formidable Chang La pass at 17,590 feet altitude. Descend into the Indus Valley, stopping to explore the grand 12-story Thiksey Monastery, famed for its striking architectural resemblance to Lhasa's Potala Palace. Also pause at the historic Shey Palace before arriving in Leh by late afternoon. Spend your final evening shopping for pashmina shawls and prayer wheels before a celebratory farewell Ladakhi dinner.

itinerary.title: Leh Farewell & Early Morning Flight Departure
itinerary.description: Enjoy an early breakfast and bid farewell to the majestic mountains of Ladakh. Your private chauffeur will transfer you to Kushok Bakula Rimpochee Airport in Leh for your morning flight back home. Gaze out of your aircraft window as you soar above endless rows of snow-clad Himalayan peaks, concluding an inspiring expedition through the rooftop of the world.

faqs.q: Is Acute Mountain Sickness (AMS) common, and how is it managed?
faqs.a: Because Leh sits at 11,500 feet, mild symptoms like light headaches can occur. Day 1 is dedicated entirely to acclimatization. We also carry medical oxygen cylinders in every vehicle and advise plenty of fluids.

faqs.q: Do I need special permits for Nubra and Pangong?
faqs.a: Yes, Inner Line Permits (ILP) are required for all domestic tourists visiting border regions like Nubra, Turtuk, and Pangong. Our operations team arranges all permits in advance, included in your package.

faqs.q: Are the luxury camps at Pangong Tso heated and comfortable?
faqs.a: Yes, our luxury partner camps at Pangong feature weather-insulated heavy canvas walls, attached private western toilets, hot water buckets, and warm thermal blankets.

faqs.q: What is the best month to book this Ladakh tour?
faqs.a: June through September is the prime window when all mountain passes including Khardung La and Chang La are clear of snow, roads are in optimal condition, and daytime weather is sunny and pleasant.

faqs.q: Can senior citizens or children join this tour?
faqs.a: Yes, healthy seniors and children above 8 years old routinely complete this tour comfortably. A routine doctor consultation regarding high altitude travel is recommended prior to booking.

faqs.q: Are pure vegetarian and Jain food options available in Ladakh?
faqs.a: Yes, all our partner resorts and luxury camps in Leh, Nubra, and Pangong provide freshly prepared pure vegetarian and Jain meals upon request.

trips.title: Royal Rajasthan (6N/7D)
trips.description: Step into the regal grandeur of the Land of Kings on an authentic journey through Rajasthan's three most fabled royal capitals: Jaipur, Jodhpur, and Udaipur. Ascend the imposing ramparts of Amber Fort in the Pink City, marvel at the intricate honeycomb façade of Hawa Mahal, and explore the astronomical wonders of Jantar Mantar. Travel west across arid desert scrubland to Jodhpur, the Blue City, where the sheer cliffside bastions of Mehrangarh Fort guard centuries of Rajput valor and Jaswant Thada's white marble shimmers. Wind south through the Aravalli hills to Udaipur, the City of Lakes. Wander through the sprawling courtyards of the City Palace, witness classical Rajasthani folk performances at Bagore Ki Haveli, and glide past the floating Lake Palace on a serene evening boat cruise across Lake Pichola. With verified heritage haveli stays, daily royal breakfasts and dinners, private air-conditioned vehicle transfers, and verified local historical guides, this journey brings Indian royal history to life with unmatched warmth.

itinerary.title: Arrival in the Pink City & Hawa Mahal Evening Exploration
itinerary.description: Arrive at Jaipur International Airport or Railway Station, where your private chauffeur welcomes you with traditional Rajasthani warmth. Transfer to your handpicked heritage haveli, adorned with ornate arches and tranquil courtyards. In the late afternoon, take a relaxed drive past the iconic pink sandstone lattice facade of Hawa Mahal (Palace of Winds). Stroll through the lively Johari Bazaar and Bapu Bazaar, savoring fragrant kachoris and browsing colorful block-printed textiles and blue pottery. Return to your haveli for a welcoming royal Rajasthani dinner by candlelit courtyards.

itinerary.title: Amber Fort Ramparts, Jal Mahal & Royal City Palace
itinerary.description: After a royal breakfast, journey to the rugged hills of Amer to explore the majestic Amber Fort. Marvel at the gleaming Sheesh Mahal (Mirror Palace) where candlelight creates a dazzling starry illusion, and admire the sweeping views over Maota Lake. Stop on your return to photograph the serene water palace of Jal Mahal resting gracefully in Man Sagar Lake. In the afternoon, visit the sprawling City Palace complex and the astronomical wonders of UNESCO World Heritage Jantar Mantar. Enjoy an authentic dinner featuring Dal Baati Churma in a heritage courtyard setting.

itinerary.title: Jaipur to Jodhpur & Mehrangarh Sunset Ramparts
itinerary.description: Depart Jaipur after breakfast on a scenic western highway drive toward the sun-drenched Thar desert fringes of Jodhpur. Arrive by early afternoon in the Blue City and check in to your heritage hotel. Head straight to the monumental Mehrangarh Fort, perched atop a 400-foot cliff, to explore its royal palanquins, weaponry museum, and vast courtyards. Watch the sun dip over the sprawling sea of indigo-blue painted houses below from the fort's western cannon ramparts. Visit nearby Jaswant Thada, the serene white marble royal cenotaph, before an evening rooftop dinner.

itinerary.title: Jodhpur to Udaipur via Ranakpur Jain Temple
itinerary.description: Enjoy breakfast before driving south through the winding Aravalli Range toward Udaipur. Break your journey at Ranakpur to marvel at the 15th-century marble Jain Temple, renowned for its 1,444 uniquely carved pillars where no two carvings are identical. Continue through lush green valleys, arriving in the romantic City of Lakes by late afternoon. Check into your lakeview hotel, unwind with refreshing spiced tea, and take an evening promenade along Fateh Sagar Lake as decorative streetlights reflect softly across the ripples. Relish a lakeside multi-course dinner under starry skies.

itinerary.title: Grand City Palace, Saheliyon Ki Bari & Sunset Pichola Cruise
itinerary.description: Spend a captivating day uncovering Udaipur's royal heritage. Begin with a guided exploration of the magnificent City Palace, the largest palace complex in Rajasthan, admiring its peacocks mosaics, glass mirror chambers, and panoramic lake balconies. Visit Saheliyon Ki Bari (Garden of the Maids of Honor) with its lotus pools and marble elephant fountains. In the late afternoon, board a private boat on Lake Pichola, gliding past Jag Mandir and the world-famous Taj Lake Palace as the setting sun bathes the palace walls in brilliant gold. Enjoy dinner overlooking the illuminated lake.

itinerary.title: Monsoon Palace Sajjangarh & Folk Cultural Evening
itinerary.description: Drive up the winding peak to the hilltop Sajjangarh Fort (Monsoon Palace), which offers dramatic 360-degree vistas across the entire lake valley and surrounding mountain sanctuaries. Spend the afternoon shopping for authentic miniature paintings, silver jewelry, and handcrafted leather journals in the quaint artisan lanes near Jagdish Temple. At dusk, witness the celebrated Dharohar Rajasthani folk dance and puppet performance at historical Bagore Ki Haveli on Gangaur Ghat, followed by a celebratory farewell dinner featuring authentic Mewari specialties.

itinerary.title: Udaipur Farewell & Airport Departure
itinerary.description: Savor your final breakfast overlooking the calm waters of Lake Pichola. Depending on your flight schedule, enjoy a relaxed morning walk around the heritage ghats or pick up last-minute handmade souvenirs and spices. Your chauffeur will assist with luggage and transfer you comfortably to Maharana Pratap Airport or Udaipur Railway Station for your flight home, concluding an unforgettable journey through the royal kingdoms of Rajasthan.

faqs.q: What is the best time of year to visit Rajasthan?
faqs.a: October through March is the ideal season, offering sunny pleasant daytime temperatures around 22°C to 26°C and cool crisp evenings, perfect for outdoor palace exploration.

faqs.q: Are the hotels authentic royal heritage properties?
faqs.a: Yes, we exclusively partner with verified heritage havelis and historic boutique palace hotels that feature traditional Rajasthani architecture, ornate jharokhas, and courtyard pools.

faqs.q: Is the Lake Pichola boat cruise included in the package?
faqs.a: Yes, standard boat cruise tickets across Lake Pichola offering close views of the Taj Lake Palace and Jag Mandir island are included in the package cost.

faqs.q: Can this itinerary be customized for different cities?
faqs.a: Absolutely. You can easily add extensions to the golden sand dunes of Jaisalmer or Pushkar by clicking the Customize Trip button on the site.

faqs.q: Is Rajasthan safe for family travel and senior citizens?
faqs.a: Rajasthan is one of the safest and most hospitable destinations in India. Our private vehicles and attentive drivers ensure senior citizens and children travel with complete comfort.

faqs.q: Are pure vegetarian and Jain meals available throughout the tour?
faqs.a: Yes, Rajasthan is world-renowned for its rich vegetarian cuisine. All our partner hotels and recommended restaurants provide authentic pure vegetarian and Jain meal preparations.

trips.title: Swiss Alpine Wonder (6N/7D)
trips.description: Immerse yourself in postcard-perfect alpine panoramas on infiYATRA's flagship holiday across Switzerland. Begin in cosmopolitan Zurich, strolling along the picturesque Limmat River and taking an excursion to Europe's most powerful waterfall, the roaring Rhine Falls. Journey along pristine lakeside rail lines to charming Lucerne, crossing the historic 14th-century wooden Chapel Bridge and ascending to the glacier paradise of Mount Titlis via the world's first revolving Rotair cable car. Continue into the Bernese Oberland heartland of Interlaken, nestled between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz. Board the iconic cogwheel railway winding up to Jungfraujoch—the Top of Europe at 3,454 meters—to step onto eternal Aletsch Glacier ice and wander through glowing Ice Palace tunnels. Featuring confirmed first-class Swiss Travel Pass passes for seamless trains and scenic lake steamers, verified four-star central hotels, daily buffet breakfasts, and expert local logistics, this journey brings alpine dreams to life with Swiss precision.

itinerary.title: Arrival in Zurich & Old Town Evening Promenade
itinerary.description: Touch down at Zurich International Airport (ZRH), where your Swiss rail host meets you with your Swiss Travel Pass. Take a smooth 12-minute train directly into Zurich Hauptbahnhof and check into your handpicked 4-star city hotel. In the late afternoon, embark on a scenic walking tour through Zurich's charming historic Altstadt (Old Town). Wander cobblestone lanes flanking the Limmat River, admire the twin Romanesque spires of Grossmünster cathedral, and stroll down world-famous Bahnhofstrasse, renowned for luxury horology and Swiss chocolatiers. Enjoy a welcoming Swiss fondue and multi-course dinner.

itinerary.title: Rhine Falls Natural Wonder & Historic Stein am Rhein
itinerary.description: After a rich buffet breakfast, take a scenic northward train to Schaffhausen to witness the roaring grandeur of the Rhine Falls, Europe's most powerful natural waterfall. Feel the spray of thunderous tumbling glacial waters on a boat ride right up to the central rock bastion in the middle of the falls. Continue to the storybook medieval village of Stein am Rhein, famous for its exceptionally preserved painted half-timbered merchant houses and peaceful riverfront cafes. Return to Zurich by late afternoon to relax by Lake Zurich before dinner.

itinerary.title: Scenic Train to Lucerne, Chapel Bridge & Lake Steamer Cruise
itinerary.description: Board a scenic morning train tracing sparkling Lake Zug toward Lucerne, nestled beneath the imposing pyramid peaks of Mount Pilatus. Check in to your lakeside hotel and explore the city on foot. Walk across the 14th-century wooden Chapel Bridge adorned with medieval ceiling paintings, visit the poignant Lion Monument carved into natural sandstone cliff, and stroll the lakeside promenade. In the late afternoon, board a historic paddle steamer for a relaxing 1-hour cruise across Lake Lucerne's fjord-like bays, admiring mountain reflections on the water before dinner.

itinerary.title: Mount Titlis Glacier Expedition: Rotair & Cliff Walk
itinerary.description: Take the scenic train to the alpine valley town of Engelberg and board a series of cable cars, culminating in the world's first revolving Titlis Rotair, which rotates a full 360 degrees as you ascend to 3,020 meters altitude. Step out onto eternal snow to cross the Titlis Cliff Walk—Europe's highest suspension bridge—hanging 500 meters above the abyss. Venture deep inside the natural Glacier Cave carved 20 meters beneath the ice surface, and ride the Ice Flyer chairlift over glacial crevasses. Return to Lucerne in the late afternoon for dinner.

itinerary.title: GoldenPass Scenic Railway to Interlaken & Grindelwald
itinerary.description: Embark on the world-renowned GoldenPass panoramic train, winding past three turquoise mountain lakes and climbing the Brunig Pass into Interlaken, the adventure hub nestled between Lake Thun and Lake Brienz. Check into your alpine hotel and take a regional train into the breathtaking glacier valley of Grindelwald. Stroll through the village under the shadow of the sheer North Face of the Eiger, taking in flower-adorned Swiss chalets and listening to cowbells echoing across meadows. Return to Interlaken for a stroll along the Hohematte park before dinner.

itinerary.title: Jungfraujoch: Top of Europe Cogwheel Train at 3,454m
itinerary.description: Prepare for the pinnacle of your Swiss holiday. Board the modern Eiger Express tricable gondola from Grindelwald Terminal, soaring directly past the Eiger North Face to Eigergletscher station. Transfer to the historic electric cogwheel train burrowing through the Eiger mountain to Jungfraujoch at 3,454 meters, Europe's highest railway station. Step out onto the Sphinx Observation Deck for jaw-dropping views of the 23-kilometer Great Aletsch Glacier, explore the illuminated Ice Palace, and visit the Lindt Swiss Chocolate Heaven before returning to Interlaken for a celebratory gala dinner.

itinerary.title: Interlaken to Zurich Airport & Departure
itinerary.description: Enjoy a relaxed Swiss breakfast featuring alpine cheeses, artisan pastries, and hot chocolate. Use your Swiss Travel Pass to board the direct intercity train from Interlaken Ost back to Zurich International Airport (ZRH). Savor final glimpses of snowy peaks, mirror-like lakes, and peaceful pastures from your comfortable panoramic carriage before boarding your international flight back home with cherished memories of Switzerland.

faqs.q: Do Indian travelers need a visa for Switzerland?
faqs.a: Yes, Indian citizens require a valid Schengen Visa. Our visa documentation desk provides personalized appointment booking assistance, verified cover letters, and insurance vouchers.

faqs.q: How does the Swiss Travel Pass work for transport?
faqs.a: The Swiss Travel Pass provides seamless hop-on hop-off access on all Swiss national trains, city trams, buses, and scenic lake ferries without having to buy separate tickets for each journey.

faqs.q: Is Jungfraujoch excursion included in the price?
faqs.a: Yes, full return tickets for the modern Eiger Express gondola and electric cogwheel train to the Top of Europe at 3,454 meters, including the Ice Palace and Sphinx Terrace, are included.

faqs.q: Can I find vegetarian and Indian food in Switzerland?
faqs.a: Yes! Switzerland is extremely welcoming to Indian travelers. Cities like Zurich, Lucerne, and Interlaken feature numerous authentic Indian restaurants as well as vegetarian-friendly cafes.

faqs.q: Is luggage transfer between cities manageable by train?
faqs.a: Yes, Swiss trains feature spacious luggage racks at coach entrances and overhead. In addition, Swiss rail offers station-to-station luggage forward services if you prefer hands-free travel.

faqs.q: What is the local currency and are credit cards accepted?
faqs.a: The currency is the Swiss Franc (CHF). International Visa and Mastercard credit and debit cards, as well as forex cards, are accepted virtually everywhere, even for minor purchases.
